us15_land.topic: Land ownership, leasing and allocation: Israel Land Authority, JNF, admissions committees; US land and zoning

claims.text: The Israel Land Authority manages 93% of the land in Israel, about 19,508,000 dunams; managed land is state, JNF or Development Authority land; the remaining 7% is privately owned or held by religious authorities.
Ownership of a home in Israel usually means a 49- or 98-year lease from the ILA; urban land is leased for 49 years with an option of a further 49.

The ILA was created in 1960 by Knesset legislation: Basic Law: Israel Lands, the Israel Lands Law, the Israel Land Administration Law (all 1960) and a 1960 covenant between the state and the World Zionist Organization/JNF.
The 2009 reform replaced the Israel Land Administration with the Israel Land Authority and converted long-term tenancy of some land into private ownership.
The Israel Land Council has 22 members: 12 from government ministries and 10 from the JNF.
A 2000 High Court ruling (Ka'adan) established that the state may not allocate land on the basis of religion or nationality, even through a third party such as the Jewish Agency.

On 26 January 2005 Attorney General Menachem Mazuz decided that ILA-managed land, including JNF-owned land, may be marketed without discrimination to Jews and non-Jews, after Adalah petitioned over a Carmiel tender from which non-Jews were barred; the JNF sought alternative land in exchange.
The JNF owns about 13% of Israel's land; Mazuz said that if a non-Jew bought JNF land, the ILA could compensate the JNF with state land; petitioners said in 2007 the ruling had not been followed.

The Admissions Committees Law (2011, amending the Cooperative Societies Ordinance) lets admissions committees in small communities in the Negev and Galilee reject applicants on grounds of social suitability; on 17 September 2014 the Supreme Court dismissed petitions against it 5-4; Adalah said it covers 434 localities.
The 2014 majority relied on ripeness: the law was not discriminatory on its face, included an anti-discrimination clause and had no concrete cases of discriminatory use yet (Fuchs, IDI).

About 90% of Arab citizens live in 139 Arab towns and villages whose jurisdiction covers less than 3% of the state's area; their population density rose 11-fold (civil-society paper citing official sources).

Knesset Research and Information Center figures: 97% of administrative demolition orders issued 2012-2014 were in the Arab sector; 97% of 1,348 judicial demolition orders in force in July 2015 were in the Arab sector.

Arab population housing need about 13,000 units a year against about 7,000 built; 2005-2009 about 20% of planned units in Arab localities (c.30,000) were marketed vs 70% in Jewish and mixed towns (c.140,000).

The Kaminitz Law, an amendment to the 1965 Planning and Building Law, was approved by the Knesset on the night of 5 April 2017; it moves enforcement powers to a national body, expands administrative demolition powers while limiting court review, and sharply raises fines; Adalah said it would have a disparate impact on Arab citizens.
About 120,000 Bedouin lived in 46 unrecognised villages in the Negev (Jerusalem Post, March 2018); Umm el-Hiran homes were destroyed in January 2017.
Government Resolution 922 (30 December 2015): announced at NIS 15bn; about NIS 10bn allocated, about NIS 6bn (62%) spent by June 2021; outline plans completed for 20 local authorities.
Resolution 550 (24 October 2021): NIS 30bn over five years; housing targets of marketing 5,000 units on state land in 2022 and up to 9,000 by 2026.

IDI (December 2025): a draft decision would move about NIS 3bn from the Resolution 550 plan to the Ministry of National Security for crime in Arab society, mostly from education, construction and housing, interior and labour budgets; an earlier 15% cut followed the outbreak of the war; IDI recommended against it and urged renewal in 2026.

The US federal government owns roughly 640 million acres, about 28% of the 2.27 billion acres of US land (data as of 30 September 2024): BLM 244.4m, Forest Service 193.1m, FWS 89.3m, NPS 80.1m, DoD 8.4m acres.
Federal land is 60.8% of Alaska, 45.9% of the 11 contiguous western states and 4.1% of all other states; Nevada 79.8%.

About 1.29 billion acres of public domain left federal ownership 1781-2024, about 816 million acres to private owners; 97% of private transfers before 1940; homestead entries peaked in 1910 at 18.3m acres; FLPMA 1976 declared remaining public domain would generally stay federal.

Euclid v. Ambler (1926): the Supreme Court held cities could use police power to exclude apartment buildings from neighbourhoods; Justice Sutherland: 'very often the apartment house is a mere parasite'.
NYT 2019 analysis: in many US cities 75% of residentially zoned land is single-family-only (San Jose 94%, New York City 15%; over 66% across California).

Reforms: Minneapolis ended single-family-only zoning December 2018; Oregon HB 2001 passed 2 July 2019; California SB 9 signed September 2021; Washington HB 1110 signed 8 May 2023; Cambridge, Massachusetts February 2025.

us15_housing.topic: Homeownership, public housing and homelessness in Israel and the US

claims.text: HUD's January 2025 point-in-time count found 745,652 people homeless, 266,320 unsheltered, a 3% decrease from 2024; HUD said homelessness rose 27% and unsheltered homelessness 36% since 2013, and chronic homelessness 81%.

HUD Secretary Scott Turner's release said the 'housing first' status quo 'has failed to meaningfully reduce homelessness' and attributed the 2025 decrease to decreases in 'Sanctuary Cities' (HUD's stated position).
US homeownership rate Q2 2026 65.0% (unchanged from Q2 2025); non-Hispanic white 74.5%, Black 45.4%, Asian/NHPI 58.6%; under-35 35.2% (36.4% a year earlier); rental vacancy 7.3%.
US homeownership peaked at 69.2% in 2004; the Q2 2026 rate is below the 25-year average of 66.3%.

Israel's public housing stock fell from about 60,000 apartments in 2014 to about 53,000 in 2019; about 10,000 were sold to tenants 2014-2019 (discounts worth NIS 3.2bn) and about 2,600 bought (NIS 3.4bn); 3,700 eligible people were waiting in 2019 with an average wait of 31 months; about 200 apartments were expected to be added.

Mehir Lamishtaken (Buyer's Price, from 2015) was replaced by Mehir Matara (Target Price), offering first-time buyers 20% off or up to NIS 300,000; its April 2022 lottery offered about 10,000 units in 31 localities and drew 119,207 registered households.

A 2022 Knesset report: Welfare Ministry aided about 2,000 homeless people in 2019 and 2,250 in 2020; local authorities treated about 3,470 in 2020 and reported about 800 more street dwellers not in treatment; shelters can house about a third.
